Load data
```{r}
# deblinding list

# add excluded tremor subjects and bind
subNo <- c(7,13,21,24,26)
excl_patients <- data.frame(subNo)
excl_patients$script_nr <- NA
excl_patients$drug_ses1 <- 'PBO' 
excl_patients$drug_ses2 <- NA
excl_patients$ses_order <- 'PBO second'

drug_list <- rbind(drug_list,excl_patients)

#read participant characteristics
#part_char <- read_delim(file.path(analysis_dir,'Participant Characteristics','input','FullData.csv'), delim = ';')
part_char <- read_excel(file.path(deriv_dir,'TableFull.xls'))
part_char$SubNr <- as.numeric(part_char$SubNr)
part_char <- part_char %>% dplyr::filter(!is.na(SubNr))

# lc_data <- read_excel(file.path(analysis_dir,'MRI','neuromelanine','output','tse_scans','LCIntensities.xlsx'))
# lc_data$SubNr <- as.numeric(lc_data$SubNr)
prop <- read.csv(file.path(deriv_dir,'Data_propranolol.csv')) %>%
  dplyr::select(subNo = Subj_ID, LC_L_prop = LC_int_L, LC_R_prop = LC_int_R)

nor <- read.csv(file.path(deriv_dir, 'nor_data_pupil.csv')) %>%
  dplyr::select(subNo, LC_L_nor = LC_L.x, LC_R_nor = LC_R.x)

# --- Combine: Data_propranolol is the default, nor_data_pupil fills any gaps ---
# Named lc_data with SubNr id column to match downstream loops/joins
lc_data <- dplyr::full_join(prop, nor, by = "subNo") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    LC_L       = dplyr::coalesce(LC_L_prop, LC_L_nor),
    LC_R       = dplyr::coalesce(LC_R_prop, LC_R_nor),
    LC_Average = rowMeans(cbind(LC_L, LC_R), na.rm = TRUE),
    LC_Average = ifelse(is.nan(LC_Average), NA, LC_Average)
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(SubNr = subNo, LC_L, LC_R, LC_Average) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(SubNr)

# read trialwise data files
cw_data <- read.csv(file.path(deriv_dir,'rawDatamat.csv'), header = F)
choice_data <- read.csv(file.path(deriv_dir,'choices_trialwise.csv'), header = F)

cw_names <- c('subNo', 'sesNo', 'dev','rt', 'setSize', 'type', 'col_pie','lureDif','thetaCorrect','tau','thetaLure' ,'signedDev','trial','block')

choice_names <- c('subNo', 'sesNo', 'type', 'setSize', 'easyOffer', 'hardOffer','choice','choiceRT','counter','adjAmt' ,'typeTask')

names(cw_data) <- cw_names
names(choice_data) <- choice_names

pupil_data <-  read.csv(file.path(deriv_dir,  'pupil_trialwise.csv'), header = TRUE)
pupil_ac <-  read.csv(file.path(deriv_dir, 'pupil_full.csv'), header = TRUE)

## ============================================================
##  OUTLIER PARTICIPANTS -- single switch for the whole script
##  Set exclude_outliers <- TRUE to drop the flagged participants from ALL
##  downstream analyses/figures; FALSE keeps everyone. Nothing else to change.
## ============================================================
exclude_outliers <- FALSE    # <<< master switch: TRUE drops outlier_ids everywhere
outlier_k        <- 3       # z cutoff for the statistical deviance rule
outlier_method   <- 'MAD'   # 'MAD' (robust median/MAD) or 'SD' (classical mean/SD)
exclude_ip_outliers <- FALSE # FALSE = flag extreme (floor/ceiling) IPs but keep them;
                             # TRUE = sensitivity analysis dropping them, per task

## Per-subject performance summaries from the raw color-wheel trials.
## `dev` is the absolute report error in degrees (0 = perfect; ~90 = chance).
perf_sub <- cw_data %>%
  dplyr::group_by(subNo) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(
    dev_easy = mean(dev[setSize == 1], na.rm = TRUE),  # set size 1 = easiest condition
    dev_all  = median(dev, na.rm = TRUE),
    rt_all   = median(rt,  na.rm = TRUE),
    n_trials = dplyr::n(),
    .groups  = 'drop')

## z-score for the statistical rule. MAD/median (default) keeps the cutoff robust
## to the very outliers being detected -- mean/SD get inflated by them (masking),
## which matters here because absolute deviance is right-skewed and bounded at
## ~90 deg. Switch to classical SD via `outlier_method <- 'SD'`. Computed on the
## EASIEST condition (genuine performers cluster tightly there, so a non-performer
## stands out most), plus overall accuracy and RT.
zfun <- function(x) {
  if (outlier_method == 'SD') (x - mean(x, na.rm = TRUE)) / sd(x, na.rm = TRUE)
  else                        (x - median(x, na.rm = TRUE)) / mad(x, na.rm = TRUE)
}
perf_sub <- perf_sub %>%
  dplyr::mutate(z_dev_easy = zfun(dev_easy), z_dev_all = zfun(dev_all), z_rt = zfun(rt_all))

## Exclusion rules -------------------------------------------------------------
## (a) Task validity: near-chance accuracy even on the easiest trials. Random
##     responding on a circular report task gives ~90 deg mean absolute error, so
##     a participant at/above that on set size 1 was not performing the task.
chance_out <- perf_sub %>% dplyr::filter(dev_easy >= 90) %>% dplyr::pull(subNo)
## (b) Statistical deviance outliers: unusually high error (z > k) on easy-trial
##     accuracy. One-sided -- only worse-than-typical performance is an outlier.
acc_out <- perf_sub %>% dplyr::filter(z_dev_easy > outlier_k) %>% dplyr::pull(subNo)
## (c) RT outliers are computed for transparency but DELIBERATELY NOT excluded:
##     in Parkinson's, tremor/bradykinesia makes slow responses expected, so a
##     long RT is not a sign of invalid data.
rt_out  <- perf_sub %>% dplyr::filter(abs(z_rt)   > outlier_k) %>% dplyr::pull(subNo)

## >>> Exclusion set = task-validity (chance) OR statistical deviance outlier.
##     RT is never used for exclusion (see (c) above).
outlier_ids <- sort(union(chance_out, acc_out))

cat('Outlier check ------------------------------------------------\n')
cat('  Method for statistical rule:', outlier_method, '(z cutoff', outlier_k, ')\n')
cat('  Near-chance accuracy (>=90 deg at set size 1) [EXCLUDED]:', paste(chance_out, collapse = ', '), '\n')
cat('  Deviance outliers (z_dev_easy >', outlier_k, ') [EXCLUDED]:', paste(acc_out, collapse = ', '), '\n')
cat('  RT outliers  (|z_rt| >',     outlier_k, ') [diagnostic, NOT excluded -- tremor]:', paste(rt_out, collapse = ', '), '\n')
cat('  exclude_outliers =', exclude_outliers, '-> excluding ids:',
    if (length(outlier_ids)) paste(outlier_ids, collapse = ', ') else '(none)', '\n')
cat('--------------------------------------------------------------\n')

if (exclude_outliers && length(outlier_ids)) {
  cw_data     <- cw_data     %>% dplyr::filter(!subNo   %in% outlier_ids)
  choice_data <- choice_data %>% dplyr::filter(!subNo   %in% outlier_ids)
  pupil_data  <- pupil_data  %>% dplyr::filter(!subject %in% outlier_ids)
  pupil_ac    <- pupil_ac    %>% dplyr::filter(!subject %in% outlier_ids)
}

## Subject-level confounds joined into the summary / pupil mixed models further
## down (age, sex, UPDRS, drug-session order). Trial-level models already carry
## these via choice_data_char / cw_t_data; these tables cover the models whose
## summary frames don't. ses_order is subject-constant (PBO first vs second).
sub_cov <- part_char %>% dplyr::transmute(
  subNo       = as.numeric(SubNr),
  Age         = as.numeric(Age),
  Gender      = factor(Gender),
  updrs_total = as.numeric(UPDRS_total))
ses_map <- drug_list %>% dplyr::distinct(subNo, ses_order)

pupil_ac_type <- pupil_ac %>% group_by(subject, drug, setSize) %>% dplyr::summarize (mean_pup =mean (mean_pup), mean_pup_enc = mean(mean_pup_enc), mean_pup_del = mean(mean_pup_del), mean_pup_int = mean(mean_pup_int) )

pupil_ac_sz <- pupil_ac %>% group_by(subject, drug, type) %>% dplyr::summarize (mean_pup =mean (mean_pup), mean_pup_enc = mean(mean_pup_enc), mean_pup_del = mean(mean_pup_del), mean_pup_int = mean(mean_pup_int) )


 pupil_drug <- pupil_ac %>% dplyr::group_by (subject,drug) %>% 
  dplyr::summarise(mean_pup = mean(mean_pup, na.rm = T), 
                   mean_pup_enc = mean(mean_pup_enc, na.rm = T), mean_pup_int = mean(mean_pup_int, na.rm = T)   )

pupil_wide <- pupil_ac  %>% pivot_wider(id_cols= c(subject), names_from = c(type,setSize,drug), values_from = c(mean_pup,mean_pup_enc,mean_pup_int, mean_pup_del))
```

Did the drug alter mood/affect (VAS / PANAS)?
```{r vas-panas-stats}
## Paired t-test PBO vs PROPRANOLOL, run separately for each affect (PANAS) and
## each factor (VAS) -- one within-subject test per subscale.
## PANAS uses the summed score per affect; VAS uses the mean score per factor (as plotted).

# drop outliers only when the master switch is on, mirroring the rest of the script
excl <- if (exclude_outliers) outlier_ids else numeric(0)
sum_panas_stat <- sum_panas %>% dplyr::filter(!Participant.Id %in% excl)
sum_vas_stat   <- sum_vas   %>% dplyr::filter(!Participant.Id %in% excl)

# paired t-test on a long frame, grouped by subscale (`grp`)
paired_drug_test <- function(df, grp, value) {
  df %>%
    dplyr::filter(drug %in% c('PBO','PROPRANOLOL')) %>%
    dplyr::select(dplyr::all_of(c(grp, 'Participant.Id', 'drug', value))) %>%
    tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = drug, values_from = dplyr::all_of(value)) %>%
    dplyr::filter(!is.na(PBO), !is.na(PROPRANOLOL)) %>%
    dplyr::group_by(dplyr::across(dplyr::all_of(grp))) %>%
    dplyr::summarise(
      n         = dplyr::n(),
      mean_PBO  = mean(PBO),
      mean_PROP = mean(PROPRANOLOL),
      mean_diff = mean(PROPRANOLOL - PBO),
      t         = t.test(PROPRANOLOL, PBO, paired = TRUE)$statistic,
      df_t      = t.test(PROPRANOLOL, PBO, paired = TRUE)$parameter,
      p         = t.test(PROPRANOLOL, PBO, paired = TRUE)$p.value,
      .groups   = 'drop')
}

cat('\n=== PANAS: PBO vs PROPRANOLOL (paired t-test, summed score by affect) ===\n')
print(as.data.frame(paired_drug_test(sum_panas_stat, 'affect', 'sum_score')))

cat('\n=== VAS: PBO vs PROPRANOLOL (paired t-test, mean score by factor) ===\n')
print(as.data.frame(paired_drug_test(sum_vas_stat, 'factor', 'mean_score')))

# Save combined VAS/PANAS drug stats for the supplement.
vas_panas_stats <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  paired_drug_test(sum_panas_stat, 'affect', 'sum_score') %>%
    dplyr::rename(subscale = affect) %>% dplyr::mutate(measure = 'PANAS', score = 'summed'),
  paired_drug_test(sum_vas_stat, 'factor', 'mean_score') %>%
    dplyr::rename(subscale = factor) %>% dplyr::mutate(measure = 'VAS', score = 'mean')) %>%
  dplyr::select(measure, subscale, n, mean_PBO, mean_PROP, mean_diff, t, df_t, p)
write.csv(vas_panas_stats, file.path(deriv_dir, 'vas_panas_drug_stats.csv'), row.names = FALSE)
print(as.data.frame(vas_panas_stats))
```

Table 1. Participant characteristics. Two descriptive columns: (1) the two-session
sample -- patients who completed the double-blind crossover with usable colour-wheel
data in BOTH sessions (the drug-analysis sample); (2) the full sample as recruited
(the two-session patients plus those excluded for an incomplete crossover or missing data).
```{r table1_td, eval=TRUE, include=TRUE}
# Two-session set = subjects with two distinct non-missing drug sessions of
# colour-wheel data (derived from the data, not hard-coded), so the count tracks
# the analysis sample. Full set = every recruited patient.
two_ses_ids <- cw_data %>% dplyr::filter(tremor_group == 'Yes', !is.na(drug), !is.na(dev)) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(subNo) %>% dplyr::summarise(n_ses = dplyr::n_distinct(drug), .groups = 'drop') %>%
  dplyr::filter(n_ses == 2) %>% dplyr::pull(subNo)
pc_td   <- part_char %>% dplyr::filter(Tremor_dominant == 'Yes')
pc_two  <- pc_td %>% dplyr::filter(as.numeric(SubNr) %in% two_ses_ids)
n_two <- nrow(pc_two); n_full <- nrow(pc_td)

fmt2 <- function(x){ x <- x[!is.na(x)]; sprintf('%.1f ± %.1f', mean(x), sd(x)) }
row2 <- function(v) c(fmt2(pc_two[[v]]), fmt2(pc_td[[v]]))
row_gender2 <- c(as.character(sum(pc_two$Gender == 'Female', na.rm = TRUE)),
                 as.character(sum(pc_td$Gender  == 'Female', na.rm = TRUE)))
table1_td <- rbind(
  'Gender, female (n)'        = row_gender2,
  'Age (years)'               = row2('Age'),
  'Disease duration (years)'  = row2('Disease_duration'),
  'MMSE'                      = row2('MMSE_score'),
  'LEDD (mg)'                 = row2('LEDD'),
  'MDS-UPDRS III (motor)'     = row2('UPDRS_total'),
  'MDS-UPDRS tremor subscore' = row2('UPDRS_total_tremor'),
  'Hoehn & Yahr'              = row2('Hoehn_and_Yahr'))
table1_td <- data.frame(Characteristic = rownames(table1_td), table1_td,
                        check.names = FALSE, row.names = NULL)
colnames(table1_td) <- c('Characteristic',
                         sprintf('Two-session sample (n = %d)', n_two),
                         sprintf('Full sample (n = %d)', n_full))
foot <- paste0("Values are mean ± SD unless otherwise noted. ",
  "MDS-UPDRS III = Movement Disorder Society Unified Parkinson's Disease Rating Scale, ",
  "motor examination (Part III); tremor subscore = sum of MDS-UPDRS III tremor items; ",
  "LEDD = levodopa-equivalent daily dose.")

# save CSV (UTF-8 so the +/- glyph survives)
con_t1 <- file(file.path(deriv_dir, 'table1_participant_characteristics.csv'), encoding = 'UTF-8')
write.csv(table1_td, con_t1, row.names = FALSE)

kt1 <- kable(table1_td, format = 'html', align = c('l', 'c', 'c'),
             caption = 'Table 1. Participant characteristics') %>%
  kable_classic(full_width = FALSE, html_font = 'Cambria', font_size = 16) %>%
  kableExtra::column_spec(1, width = '5cm') %>%
  kableExtra::footnote(general = foot, general_title = "Note. ", footnote_as_chunk = TRUE)
# render PNG (guarded: a webshot/phantomjs failure must not abort the knit)
tryCatch({
  tmp1 <- tempfile(fileext = '.html')
  # left-align the caption/title so it matches the other (sjPlot) tables, and add a
  # horizontal rule directly under the title (separating it from the table body)
  full1 <- paste0('<!DOCTYPE html><html><head><meta charset="utf-8">',
                  '<style>caption{text-align:left !important;padding-left:0;',
                  'border-bottom:1.5px solid #000;padding-bottom:5px;margin-bottom:2px;}',
                  'tfoot td{border-top:1.5px solid #000 !important;padding-top:5px;}</style></head><body>',
                  as.character(kt1), '</body></html>')
  c1 <- file(tmp1, encoding = 'UTF-8'); writeLines(full1, c1, useBytes = FALSE); close(c1)
  webshot::webshot(paste0('file:///', gsub('\\\\', '/', normalizePath(tmp1))),
                   file.path(deriv_dir, 'figures', 'table1_participant_characteristics.png'),
                   zoom = 2, selector = 'table')
  unlink(tmp1)
}, error = function(err) cat('Table 1 PNG render skipped:', conditionMessage(err), '\n'))
kt1
```

Choices analysis
```{r}
## type task: (1:8, 1:i1-i3, 2: u1-u3, 3: i1-u1, 4: i3-u3, 5: i1-nr, 6: i3-nr, 6: u1-nr 8: u3-nr)

choice_data <- choice_data %>% mutate(type = dplyr::recode(type, '0' = 'Ignore', '2' = 'Update')) %>% dplyr::filter(!is.na(choice)) %>%  dplyr::mutate(task_name = case_when(typeTask <= 2 ~ 'sz', typeTask == 3 | typeTask == 4 ~ 'dir', typeTask >= 5 ~ 'nr' ), session_nr = case_when(ses_order == 'PBO first' & drug == 'PBO' ~ 1, ses_order == 'PBO second' & drug == 'PROPRANOLOL' ~1, is.na(ses_order) ~ 1, TRUE ~ 2))

ip_long <- choice_data %>% dplyr::group_by (subNo,drug,task_name,type,setSize) %>% dplyr::filter (counter == max(`counter`)) %>% dplyr::summarise(IP = case_when(choice == 1 ~ easyOffer- adjAmt/2, choice == 0 ~ easyOffer+ adjAmt/2), tremor_group = getmode(tremor_group), ses_order = getmode(ses_order),session_nr = getmode(sesNo))

## ---- IP extreme-value flag (per task) ----
## An IP at the floor/ceiling of the offer range can mean EITHER a non-converged
## staircase OR a genuine extreme preference (always avoid / always take effort) --
## the two are indistinguishable from the IP alone, and a real extreme preference
## may be the effect of interest. So extreme IPs are FLAGGED for transparency but
## KEPT in the primary analysis. Flip exclude_ip_outliers to TRUE only to run a
## sensitivity analysis. The flag is per (subNo, task_name), applied task-specific
## (a participant's extreme IP on one task does not remove their other tasks).
ip_lo <- 0.25; ip_hi <- 3.75   # offer range is ~0.09-3.9; these catch the rails
ip_flag <- ip_long %>% dplyr::group_by(subNo, task_name) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(mean_IP = mean(IP, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = 'drop') %>%
  dplyr::mutate(ip_extreme = mean_IP <= ip_lo | mean_IP >= ip_hi)
cat('IP extreme-value flags per task (kept unless exclude_ip_outliers = TRUE):\n')
print(as.data.frame(dplyr::filter(ip_flag, ip_extreme)))
ip_excl <- ip_flag %>% dplyr::filter(ip_extreme) %>% dplyr::select(subNo, task_name)
if (exclude_ip_outliers && nrow(ip_excl) > 0) {
  ip_long <- ip_long %>% dplyr::anti_join(ip_excl, by = c('subNo', 'task_name'))
}

ip_long_nr <- ip_long %>% dplyr::filter(task_name == 'nr' & !is.na(drug))
  
ratio_long_nr <- choice_data %>% filter(task_name =='nr') %>% dplyr::group_by (subNo,drug,type,setSize) %>% dplyr::summarise(ratio_redo = sum(choice)/5 )

ratio_long_nr_type_drug <- choice_data %>% filter(task_name =='nr') %>% dplyr::group_by (subNo,drug,type) %>% dplyr::summarise(ratio_redo = sum(choice)/10 )

auc_nr <- ip_long_nr %>% dplyr::summarise(auc_nr = DescTools::AUC(as.numeric(setSize), IP)) 

ip_wide_nr <- ip_long_nr %>% pivot_wider(id_cols= subNo, names_from = c(type, setSize,drug), values_from = IP)

ip_wide_dir <- ip_long %>% dplyr::filter(task_name == 'dir' & !is.na(drug)) %>% pivot_wider(id_cols= subNo, names_from = c(setSize,drug), values_from = IP, names_prefix='sz') %>% dplyr::mutate(sz1_effect = sz1_PROPRANOLOL - sz1_PBO, sz3_effect = sz3_PROPRANOLOL - sz3_PBO, sz_effect = sz3_effect - sz1_effect )

ip_wide_sz <- ip_long %>% dplyr::filter(task_name == 'sz' & !is.na(drug)) %>% pivot_wider(id_cols= subNo, names_from = c(type,drug), values_from = IP)

ip_wide_tremor <- ip_long %>% dplyr::filter(!is.na(drug)) %>% group_by (task_name) %>% pivot_wider(id_cols= c(subNo,tremor_group, ses_order), names_from = c(task_name, type, setSize, drug), values_from = IP)

ip_wide <- inner_join(ip_wide_nr,ip_wide_dir, by='subNo') %>% inner_join(., ip_wide_sz, by = 'subNo')

write.csv(choice_data,file.path(deriv_dir, 'raw_choice_data_drug.csv'), row.names = FALSE)
```

Mixed model: predict deviance drug effects
```{r}

cw_data_char <- inner_join(cw_data,part_char, by = c( 'subNo' = 'SubNr')) %>% left_join(., pupil_data, by = c('subNo' = 'subject', 'sesNo' = 'session','trial' ))
  
  #stops installation questions
options(buildtools.check = function(action) TRUE)
cw_t_data <- cw_data_char %>% dplyr::filter(tremor_group=='Yes') %>% dplyr::mutate(
  updrs_total_z = ave(updrs_total, FUN = scale), 
  age_z = ave(Age, FUN = scale),
  lc_average_z = ave(lc_average, FUN = scale), 
  mean_pup_int_z =  ave(mean_pup_int, FUN = scale),
  mean_pup_z = ave(mean_pup, FUN = scale),
  mean_pup_enc_z = ave(mean_pup_enc, FUN = scale))

## Complete-session restriction for DRUG models: keep only subjects with BOTH drug
## conditions (the within-subject crossover). Applied via only_cs() at each drug
## model's data = argument. Drug-INDEPENDENT analyses (ribbons, PBO descriptives,
## group comparisons) keep the full frames. All drug models use (1+drug_dev|subNo).
only_cs <- function(df) df %>% dplyr::group_by(subNo) %>%
  dplyr::filter(dplyr::n_distinct(drug[!is.na(drug)]) == 2) %>% dplyr::ungroup()

## Deviation (sum-to-zero, ±0.5) coding of the design factors. Using these in the
## models makes every lower-order coefficient a MARGINAL main effect (averaged over
## the other factors) rather than a simple effect at an arbitrary reference / at
## setSize = 0 -- so the make_tab coefficient tables report the correct main-effect
## p-values directly. This is a reparameterisation: model fit, predictions and all
## interaction tests are identical; only the coefficient rows become interpretable.
## Direction of each contrast (high level = +0.5): effort_dev = high vs low load;
## type_dev = Update vs Ignore; drug_dev = propranolol vs placebo; task_dev =
## no-effort-vs-effort vs low-vs-high-effort. Original factor columns are kept for
## figures and for the emmeans simple-effects (drug within Ignore/Update).
add_dev <- function(df) {
  df$drug_dev   <- ifelse(as.character(df$drug) == 'PROPRANOLOL', 0.5, -0.5)
  if ('type' %in% names(df))        df$type_dev   <- ifelse(as.character(df$type) == 'Update', 0.5, -0.5)
  if ('setSize' %in% names(df))     df$effort_dev <- ifelse(df$setSize == 3, 0.5, -0.5)
  if ('effort_task' %in% names(df)) df$task_dev   <- ifelse(as.character(df$effort_task) == 'No-effort vs effort', 0.5, -0.5)
  df
}

 devL <- lmer(dev ~ effort_dev*type_dev*drug_dev+ updrs_total_z +ses_order+Gender + age_z + mean_pup_int_z+(1+drug_dev|subNo),data = add_dev(only_cs(cw_t_data)), control = lmerControl(optimizer = 'Nelder_Mead', optCtrl = list(maxfun = 100000000)))
  
  prefix='deviance_drug_lmer'

 save("devL", file = file.path(deriv_dir, sprintf("%s.RData",'deviance_drug_lmer')))

  dv_labels <- 'Performance error'


#findBetas(devTrMl)
```

Mixed model: predict choice no redo tremor, drug effects
```{r echo=TRUE}

choice_data_char <- inner_join(choice_data,part_char, by = c( 'subNo' = 'SubNr')) 


  #stops installation questions
options(buildtools.check = function(action) TRUE)

nr_tr_choice_data <-choice_data_char %>% dplyr::filter(tremor_group=='Yes', typeTask>=5) %>% dplyr::inner_join(., pupil_ac, by = c('subNo' = 'subject', 'drug',  'type', 'setSize'))%>% dplyr::left_join(., cw_long %>% dplyr::select(subNo, drug, median_dev, type, setSize), by = c('subNo','drug', 'type','setSize'))

choiceLp <- glmer(choice ~ drug_dev+scale(mean_pup, scale = T)+effort_dev+type_dev+scale(median_dev, scale=T)+scale(updrs_total, scale = T)+scale(easyOffer, scale = T)+scale(Age,scale = T)+Gender+ses_order+(1+drug_dev|subNo),data = add_dev(only_cs(nr_tr_choice_data)), family = binomial,  control = glmerControl(optimizer = 'Nelder_Mead', optCtrl = list(maxfun = 1000000000000000)))

 summary(choiceLp)
    prefix='choice_tremor'
  save("choiceLp", file = file.path(deriv_dir, sprintf("%s.RData",prefix)))
  
# Match the performance models' structure: the no-redo (nr) task varies both
# setSize and type, so include the full effort_dev*type_dev*drug_dev interaction.
# Random effects: maximal supported by the data (the full 3-way random slope is
# singular); (1+drug_dev|subNo) is the richest that converges non-singular.
# WM-task deviance (performance error) as a per-cell covariate, matched to the
# factors this model includes (setSize x type x drug): median WM deviance in cell.
nr_tr_choice_data <- nr_tr_choice_data %>% dplyr::left_join(
  cw_t_data %>% dplyr::group_by(subNo, setSize, type, drug) %>%
    dplyr::summarise(wm_dev = median(dev, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = 'drop'),
  by = c('subNo', 'setSize', 'type', 'drug'))
# median_dev dropped (was only in this model); covariates harmonized across all
# choice models so Age/UPDRS/easy offer collapse to single rows in the combined table.
choiceLNp <- glmer(choice ~ effort_dev*type_dev*drug_dev + scale(easyOffer)+scale(updrs_total)+scale(Age)+Gender+ses_order+scale(wm_dev) + (1+drug_dev|subNo),data = add_dev(only_cs(nr_tr_choice_data)), family = binomial,  control = glmerControl(optimizer = 'bobyqa', optCtrl = list(maxfun = 2e5)))
```

Pupil during working memory predicts subsequent high-effort choice (tremor-dominant)
```{r pupil_predicts_choice_TD, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
## Does pupil DURING the WM task predict subsequently CHOOSING the higher-effort option?
## TREMOR-DOMINANT, PBO session only (one observation per subject -- the placebo/baseline
## session, so the pupil-choice relationship is characterised without the drug manipulation;
## including the propranolol session attenuates it). Three decision types, reported together in
## one table for consistency with the other analyses: no-redo (nr, effort vs no effort),
## set-size (sz, low vs high effort), and the two pooled (merged). Outcome chose_high_effort =
## as.integer(choice == 0). Pupil is z-scored WITHIN SESSION (pupil_cells_wz.csv) and joined at
## each design's granularity (nr: setSize x type; sz/merged: type). INTERACTION spec: pupil
## interacts with the deviation-coded (±0.5) design factors, so the scale(pupil) main term is the
## MARGINAL pupil effect (the table's Pupil row = the reported number). Task-type is dropped from
## the encoding/delay models (the two task-types are physically identical until interference).
pupphases_pc <- c('wz_whole', 'wz_enc', 'wz_del', 'wz_int')
cells_wz_pc  <- read.csv(file.path(deriv_dir, 'pupil_cells_wz.csv'))
pc_cov_pc <- part_char %>% dplyr::transmute(subNo = as.numeric(SubNr),
  updrs_tot = as.numeric(UPDRS_total), Age = as.numeric(Age), Gender = Gender)
# pupil aggregated to each design's granularity
pup_nr_g <- cells_wz_pc %>% dplyr::group_by(subject, session, setSize, type) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(dplyr::across(dplyr::all_of(pupphases_pc), ~mean(.x, na.rm = TRUE)), .groups = 'drop')
pup_ty_g <- cells_wz_pc %>% dplyr::group_by(subject, session, type) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(dplyr::across(dplyr::all_of(pupphases_pc), ~mean(.x, na.rm = TRUE)), .groups = 'drop')
# base = TD, PBO session, with covariates and the high-effort outcome
base_pc_td <- choice_data %>%
  dplyr::filter(tremor_group == 'Yes', drug == 'PBO', !is.na(choice)) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(chose_high_effort = as.integer(choice == 0)) %>%
  dplyr::left_join(pc_cov_pc, by = 'subNo')
add_dev_pc <- function(df){
  if ('setSize' %in% names(df))     df$effort_dev <- ifelse(df$setSize == 3, 0.5, -0.5)
  if ('type' %in% names(df))        df$type_dev   <- ifelse(as.character(df$type) == 'Update', 0.5, -0.5)
  if ('effort_task' %in% names(df)) df$task_dev   <- ifelse(as.character(df$effort_task) == 'sz', 0.5, -0.5)
  df }
nr_pc_td <- add_dev_pc(base_pc_td %>% dplyr::filter(task_name == 'nr') %>%
  dplyr::left_join(pup_nr_g, by = c('subNo'='subject','sesNo'='session','setSize','type')))
sz_pc_td <- add_dev_pc(base_pc_td %>% dplyr::filter(task_name == 'sz') %>%
  dplyr::left_join(pup_ty_g, by = c('subNo'='subject','sesNo'='session','type')))
mg_pc_td <- add_dev_pc(base_pc_td %>% dplyr::filter(task_name %in% c('nr','sz')) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(effort_task = task_name) %>%
  dplyr::left_join(pup_ty_g, by = c('subNo'='subject','sesNo'='session','type')))

gctrl_pc <- glmerControl(optimizer = 'bobyqa', optCtrl = list(maxfun = 2e5))
specs_pc <- list('Effort vs no effort' = list(df = nr_pc_td, design = 'effort_dev*type_dev'),
                 'High vs low effort'  = list(df = sz_pc_td, design = 'type_dev'),
                 'Merged'              = list(df = mg_pc_td, design = 'task_dev*type_dev'))
# type only meaningful once interference stimuli appear -> stripped from encoding/delay
strip_type_pc <- function(d){ p <- trimws(strsplit(d, '\\*')[[1]]); p <- p[p != 'type_dev']
  if (length(p) == 0) '1' else paste(p, collapse = '*') }
design_for_pc <- function(design, pv) if (pv %in% c('wz_enc','wz_del')) strip_type_pc(design) else design
fit_pc <- function(df, design, pv){
  d <- df %>% dplyr::mutate(pupil = .data[[pv]])
  interact <- if (design == '1') 'scale(pupil)' else paste0('scale(pupil)*', design)
  f <- paste0('chose_high_effort ~ ', interact,
              ' + scale(easyOffer) + scale(updrs_tot) + scale(Age) + Gender + (1|subNo)')
  glmer(as.formula(f), data = d, family = binomial, control = gctrl_pc)
}

# --- MAIN TABLE: whole-trial pupil, one column per decision type (nr / sz / merged) ---
main_TD_pc <- lapply(specs_pc, function(s) fit_pc(s$df, s$design, 'wz_whole'))
save(main_TD_pc, file = file.path(deriv_dir, 'pupil_choice_main_TD.RData'))
cat('\n=== Pupil -> high-effort choice (tremor-dominant, PBO): whole-trial marginal pupil ===\n')
for (nm in names(specs_pc)) { d <- specs_pc[[nm]]$df %>% dplyr::filter(!is.na(wz_whole))
  co <- summary(main_TD_pc[[nm]])$coefficients; r <- 'scale(pupil)'
  cat(sprintf('  %-20s subj=%d decisions=%d  OR=%.3f [%.3f, %.3f]  z=%.2f  p=%.4g\n', nm,
      dplyr::n_distinct(d$subNo), nrow(d),
      exp(co[r,1]), exp(co[r,1]-1.96*co[r,2]), exp(co[r,1]+1.96*co[r,2]),
      co[r,3], 2*pnorm(-abs(co[r,3])))) }
wins_pc <- c(Encoding = 'wz_enc', Delay = 'wz_del', Interference = 'wz_int', 'Whole trial' = 'wz_whole')

# --- MAIN Table 5: no-redo (effort vs no effort) pupil -> choice, by working-memory phase.
# The headline of this exploratory analysis is that WM pupil predicts subsequent effort
# choice; the no-redo decisions carry it, so the MAIN table shows the no-redo effect resolved
# across phases (Encoding, Delay, Interference, Whole trial). Task-type is dropped from the
# encoding/delay models (the two task-types are physically identical until interference). ---
nr_by_win <- lapply(names(wins_pc), function(w) fit_pc(nr_pc_td, design_for_pc('effort_dev*type_dev', wins_pc[[w]]), wins_pc[[w]]))
make_tab(model = nr_by_win, directory = deriv_dir,
         title = 'Table 5. Pupil predicts high-effort choice (no-redo) by working-memory phase',
         dv_labels = names(wins_pc))

# --- SUPPLEMENT (cross-task comparison, so the reader can see the effect is not shown for
# the other decisions because it is undetectable there, NOT because it was omitted): the three
# decision types (no-redo / set-size / merged) compared at the WHOLE-TRIAL ('average') pupil
# and at the DELAY window (where even the pooled effect was reliable). main_TD_pc = whole-trial. ---
make_tab(model = unname(main_TD_pc), directory = deriv_dir,
         title = 'Supplemental Table 4. Pupil predicts high-effort choice by decision type (whole-trial pupil)',
         dv_labels = names(specs_pc))
delay_by_task <- lapply(names(specs_pc), function(nm) fit_pc(specs_pc[[nm]]$df, design_for_pc(specs_pc[[nm]]$design, 'wz_del'), 'wz_del'))
make_tab(model = delay_by_task, directory = deriv_dir,
         title = 'Supplemental Table 5. Pupil predicts high-effort choice by decision type (delay-window pupil)',
         dv_labels = names(specs_pc))

# --- internal record: marginal pupil OR by decision type x window (all cells, for the text) ---
pc_phase_td <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(specs_pc), function(nm){
  do.call(rbind, lapply(names(wins_pc), function(w){ pv <- wins_pc[[w]]
    m  <- fit_pc(specs_pc[[nm]]$df, design_for_pc(specs_pc[[nm]]$design, pv), pv)
    co <- summary(m)$coefficients; r <- 'scale(pupil)'
    data.frame(decision = nm, window = w, OR = round(exp(co[r,1]), 3),
               CI = sprintf('[%.2f, %.2f]', exp(co[r,1]-1.96*co[r,2]), exp(co[r,1]+1.96*co[r,2])),
               z = round(co[r,3], 2), p = round(2*pnorm(-abs(co[r,3])), 4),
               row.names = NULL) })) }))
cat('\n=== Pupil -> high-effort choice (tremor-dominant, PBO): by decision type x window ===\n')
print(pc_phase_td)
write.csv(pc_phase_td, file.path(deriv_dir, 'pupil_choice_TD_phase_summary.csv'), row.names = FALSE)

# --- Figure 3D: model-predicted P(chose the higher-effort option) across the within-session
# pupil range (no-redo decisions). Predictors are pre-scaled; design factors held at their
# deviation-coded centre (marginal effect), covariates at their mean,
# Gender at reference; population-level (fixed-effects) fit with a delta-method 95% CI; the
# x-axis is back-transformed to the within-session z pupil scale. ---
predict_pc_td <- function(df, design){
  d <- df %>% dplyr::filter(is.finite(wz_whole)) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(pupz = as.numeric(scale(wz_whole)),
                  eoz = as.numeric(scale(easyOffer)), untz = as.numeric(scale(updrs_tot)),
                  agez = as.numeric(scale(Age)), Gender = factor(Gender))
  mu <- mean(d$wz_whole, na.rm = TRUE); sdv <- sd(d$wz_whole, na.rm = TRUE)
  interact <- if (design == '1') 'pupz' else paste0('pupz*', design)
  m <- glmer(as.formula(paste0('chose_high_effort ~ ', interact, ' + eoz + untz + agez + Gender + (1|subNo)')),
             data = d, family = binomial, control = gctrl_pc)
  dvterms <- setdiff(trimws(unlist(strsplit(design, '[*]'))), '1')
  g0 <- list(pupz = seq(quantile(d$pupz, .02, na.rm = TRUE), quantile(d$pupz, .98, na.rm = TRUE), length = 80),
             eoz = 0, untz = 0, agez = 0, Gender = factor(levels(d$Gender)[1], levels = levels(d$Gender)))
  for (tt in dvterms) g0[[tt]] <- 0
  grid <- do.call(expand.grid, g0)
  eta <- as.numeric(predict(m, newdata = grid, re.form = NA, type = 'link'))
  X <- model.matrix(delete.response(terms(lme4::nobars(formula(m)))), grid)
  beta <- lme4::fixef(m); V <- as.matrix(vcov(m))
  keep <- intersect(names(beta), colnames(X)); X <- X[, keep, drop = FALSE]; V <- V[keep, keep, drop = FALSE]
  se <- sqrt(rowSums((X %*% V) * X))
  grid %>% dplyr::mutate(pupil = pupz * sdv + mu, fit = plogis(eta),
                         lo = plogis(eta - 1.96 * se), hi = plogis(eta + 1.96 * se))
}
# primary: no-redo (effort-vs-no-effort), the significant effect
pred_nr_td <- predict_pc_td(nr_pc_td, 'effort_dev*type_dev')
fig5_td <- ggplot(pred_nr_td, aes(pupil, fit)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), alpha = .18, fill = '#126192') +
  geom_line(colour = '#126192', linewidth = 1.1) + theme_classic() +
  labs(x = 'Pupil during working memory (within-session z)',
       y = 'Predicted P(chose higher-effort option)') +
  theme(axis.title = element_text(size = 13))
print(fig5_td)
ggsave(file.path(deriv_dir, 'figures', 'pupil_choice_predicted_TD.pdf'), plot = fig5_td, height = 4.2, width = 6)
ggsave(file.path(deriv_dir, 'figures', 'pupil_choice_predicted_TD.png'), plot = fig5_td, height = 4.2, width = 6, dpi = 120)
```

Drug effect on pupil (z-scored and raw)
```{r}
# ---- Drug effect on pupil ---------------------------------------------------
# Finalised with a pipeline consistent with the WM performance models: fit on the
# SAME trial-level frame (cw_t_data = tremor patients, both drug sessions), the
# SAME effort_dev*type_dev*drug_dev fixed structure, the SAME additive covariates, and the
# SAME maximal-supported (1+drug_dev|subNo) random-effects protocol as devL/rtL
# (reduce to (1|subNo) only when the maximal model is singular). Pupil is the DV
# here, so mean_pup_int is NOT entered as a covariate. Fit for every phase
# (whole-trial, encoding, delay, interference), both z-scored (within session)
# and raw; z and raw are kept in two separate tables.

fit_pupil <- function(dv) {
  base <- paste0(dv, " ~ effort_dev*type_dev*drug_dev + updrs_total_z + ses_order + Gender + age_z + ")
  ctrl <- lmerControl(optimizer = 'Nelder_Mead', optCtrl = list(maxfun = 1e8))
  m <- lmer(as.formula(paste0(base, "(1+drug_dev|subNo)")), data = add_dev(only_cs(cw_t_data)), control = ctrl)
  if (isSingular(m))  # parsimonious reduction, same rule as the other drug models
    m <- lmer(as.formula(paste0(base, "(1|subNo)")), data = add_dev(only_cs(cw_t_data)), control = ctrl)
  m
}

# z-scored (within-session) pupil, per phase
pupil_z_whole <- fit_pupil('mean_pup')
pupil_z_enc   <- fit_pupil('mean_pup_enc')
pupil_z_del   <- fit_pupil('mean_pup_del')
pupil_z_int   <- fit_pupil('mean_pup_int')

# raw pupil, per phase
pupil_raw_whole <- fit_pupil('mean_raw_pup')
pupil_raw_enc   <- fit_pupil('mean_raw_pup_enc')
pupil_raw_del   <- fit_pupil('mean_raw_pup_del')
pupil_raw_int   <- fit_pupil('mean_raw_pup_int')

save(pupil_z_whole, pupil_z_enc, pupil_z_del, pupil_z_int,
     pupil_raw_whole, pupil_raw_enc, pupil_raw_del, pupil_raw_int,
     file = file.path(deriv_dir, 'pupil_drug.RData'))

# One table (z-scored, within-session): mean (whole trial) + the three task phases side
# by side. The raw-scaling table was dropped -- z-scored (size-normalised) is the primary
# and only reported pupil metric; the raw fits are still computed above for the record.
make_tab(model = list(pupil_z_whole, pupil_z_enc, pupil_z_del, pupil_z_int),
         title = 'Table 4. Pupil drug effects', directory = deriv_dir,
         dv_labels = c('Mean', 'Encoding', 'Delay', 'Interference'))

# --- raw per-session pupil frame (used by the pupil figures below). Map session -> drug.
both_drug <- pupil_ac %>% dplyr::filter(!is.na(drug)) %>% dplyr::distinct(subject, drug) %>%
  dplyr::count(subject) %>% dplyr::filter(n == 2) %>% dplyr::pull(subject)

drug_long <- drug_list %>% dplyr::select(subNo, drug_ses1, drug_ses2) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_longer(c(drug_ses1, drug_ses2), names_to = 'session', values_to = 'drug',
                      names_pattern = 'drug_ses(.)') %>%
  dplyr::mutate(session = as.integer(session))

pup_raw_ses <- read.csv(file.path(deriv_dir, 'pupil_full_ses.csv')) %>%
  dplyr::left_join(drug_long, by = c('subject' = 'subNo', 'session')) %>%
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(drug), subject %in% both_drug) %>%
  dplyr::left_join(sub_cov, by = c('subject' = 'subNo')) %>%
  dplyr::left_join(ses_map, by = c('subject' = 'subNo'))
```

Low vs high effort choice tremor
```{r}

  #stops installation questions
options(buildtools.check = function(action) TRUE)

sz_tr_choice_data <-choice_data_char %>% dplyr::filter(tremor_group=='Yes', typeTask <=2)

sz_tr_choice_data <- sz_tr_choice_data %>% dplyr::mutate(easyOfferZ = (easyOffer - mean(easyOffer))/sd(easyOffer))

 # choiceSZTrM <- brm(choice~scale(easyOffer)+drug_dev*type_dev+scale(Age)+ses_order+(1+drug_dev|subNo),data = add_dev(only_cs(sz_tr_choice_data)),  family = 'bernoulli', cores = getOption("mc.cores", 8), warmup = 1000, iter = 2000, chains = 6,control = list(adapt_delta = 0.99))
 #  summary(choiceSZTrM)
  
# Random effects: maximal structure supported by the data. drug_dev*type_dev is the tested
# within-subject interaction, so include its random slope: (1+drug_dev|subNo)
# converges non-singular. NB this is more conservative than (1+drug_dev|subNo): it
# moves the drug x type interaction from p=.008 (anti-conservative) to a trend
# (p=.14); the drug simple effect at Ignore stays significant (OR 0.33, p=.035).
## WM-task deviance (performance error) per cell matched to this model's factors
## (type x drug; setSize is the choice dimension here so it cannot enter). Controls
## for WM performance -- the covariate is deviance (which the drug affects), not RT
## (which it does not) -- so the effort effect is not explained by WM performance.
sz_tr_choice_data <- sz_tr_choice_data %>% dplyr::left_join(
  cw_t_data %>% dplyr::group_by(subNo, type, drug) %>%
    dplyr::summarise(wm_dev = median(dev, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = 'drop'),
  by = c('subNo', 'type', 'drug'))
choice_sz_TrLm <- glmer(choice ~ drug_dev*type_dev + scale(easyOffer)+scale(updrs_total)+scale(Age)+Gender+ses_order+scale(wm_dev) + (1+drug_dev|subNo),data = add_dev(only_cs(sz_tr_choice_data)), family = binomial,  control = glmerControl(optimizer = 'bobyqa', optCtrl = list(maxfun = 2e5)))

tab_model(choice_sz_TrLm)


# --- Verify the drug x task-type interaction with a model-free, subject-level test ---
# Aggregate each subject's P(choose the higher set size) per drug x type, then test the
# drug effect (PROPRANOLOL - PBO) within each task-type with a paired t-test. This
# confirms the glmer interaction without relying on its link function or optimizer.
# (choice==1 = chose the LOW set size, so chose_high = choice==0.)
sz_high <- sz_tr_choice_data %>%
  dplyr::mutate(chose_high = as.integer(choice == 0)) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(subNo, drug, type) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(p_high = mean(chose_high), .groups = 'drop')
cat('\n=== sz: mean P(choose high set size) by drug x task-type ===\n')
print(as.data.frame(sz_high %>% dplyr::group_by(drug, type) %>%
                      dplyr::summarise(p_high = mean(p_high), .groups = 'drop')))
sz_wide <- sz_high %>% tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = drug, values_from = p_high)
cat('\n=== sz: drug effect (PROPRANOLOL - PBO) within each task-type (paired t-test) ===\n')
for (ty in sort(unique(as.character(sz_wide$type)))) {
  d <- dplyr::filter(sz_wide, type == ty)
  d <- d[stats::complete.cases(d[, c('PBO', 'PROPRANOLOL')]), ]
  tt <- t.test(d$PROPRANOLOL, d$PBO, paired = TRUE)
  cat(sprintf('  %-7s: diff = %+.3f, t(%d) = %.2f, p = %.3f (n = %d)\n',
              ty, mean(d$PROPRANOLOL - d$PBO),
              tt$parameter, tt$statistic, tt$p.value, nrow(d)))
}

  prefix='choice_sz_tremor'

  save("choice_sz_TrLm", file = file.path(deriv_dir, sprintf("%s.RData",prefix)))


# =====================================================================================
# Direct-comparison validation of the nr task-type effect (TD patients, placebo only)
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# In the no-redo (nr) task there is a task-type effect: TD patients redo the WM task
# (choice==0 = chose to exert effort) MORE for Update than for Ignore trials. A
# model-free validation is to look at the DIRECT (dir) comparison, where Ignore and
# Update are pitted against each other in the same trial. Task design: the a-priori
# higher-effort offer was always FIXED at 2 (in dir that offer is Ignore; the Update
# offer was titrated), so choice==0 = chose Ignore and choice==1 = chose Update. We make
# no claim about which option is subjectively more effortful for these patients — the
# labels below are the task's Ignore/Update conditions only.
# Because dir is a staircase, the raw choice proportion is compressed toward 0.5, so we
# report BOTH P(chose Ignore) and the indifference point (IP) of the titrated Update
# offer relative to the fixed Ignore offer (2): IP < 2 means Update was chosen even when
# it paid less than Ignore, i.e. Update was preferred.
cat('\n===== Direct-comparison validation of the nr task-type effect (TD, PBO) =====\n')

# (1) nr: P(chose to exert effort / redo) by task-type, paired Ignore vs Update
nr_eff_pbo <- choice_data_char %>%
  dplyr::filter(tremor_group == 'Yes', typeTask >= 5, drug == 'PBO', !is.na(choice)) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(chose_effort = as.integer(choice == 0)) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(subNo, type) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(p_eff = mean(chose_effort), .groups = 'drop')
cat('\n[nr] mean P(chose to redo / exert effort) by task-type:\n')
print(as.data.frame(nr_eff_pbo %>% dplyr::group_by(type) %>%
                      dplyr::summarise(p_eff = mean(p_eff), .groups = 'drop')))
nr_eff_wide <- nr_eff_pbo %>% tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = type, values_from = p_eff)
nr_eff_wide <- nr_eff_wide[stats::complete.cases(nr_eff_wide[, c('Ignore', 'Update')]), ]
tt_nr <- t.test(nr_eff_wide$Ignore, nr_eff_wide$Update, paired = TRUE)
cat(sprintf('[nr] Ignore - Update = %+.3f, t(%d) = %.2f, p = %.3f (n = %d)\n',
            mean(nr_eff_wide$Ignore - nr_eff_wide$Update),
            tt_nr$parameter, tt_nr$statistic, tt_nr$p.value, nrow(nr_eff_wide)))

# (2) dir: P(chose Ignore over Update), one-sample vs 0.5
dir_ign_pbo <- choice_data_char %>%
  dplyr::filter(tremor_group == 'Yes', typeTask %in% c(3, 4), drug == 'PBO', !is.na(choice)) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(chose_ignore = as.integer(choice == 0)) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(subNo) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(p_ignore = mean(chose_ignore), .groups = 'drop')
tt_dir <- t.test(dir_ign_pbo$p_ignore, mu = 0.5)
cat(sprintf('\n[dir] P(chose Ignore over Update) = %.3f vs 0.5, t(%d) = %.2f, p = %.3f (n = %d)\n',
            mean(dir_ign_pbo$p_ignore), tt_dir$parameter, tt_dir$statistic,
            tt_dir$p.value, nrow(dir_ign_pbo)))

# (3) dir: indifference point of the titrated Update offer vs the fixed Ignore offer (2)
dir_ip_pbo <- ip_long %>%
  dplyr::filter(task_name == 'dir', tremor_group == 'Yes', drug == 'PBO') %>%
  dplyr::group_by(subNo) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(IP = mean(IP, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = 'drop')
tt_ip <- t.test(dir_ip_pbo$IP, mu = 2)
cat(sprintf('[dir] Update-vs-Ignore IP = %.3f vs 2 (fixed Ignore offer), t(%d) = %.2f, p = %.3f (n = %d)\n',
            mean(dir_ip_pbo$IP, na.rm = TRUE), tt_ip$parameter, tt_ip$statistic,
            tt_ip$p.value, nrow(dir_ip_pbo)))
cat('  (IP < 2 => Update chosen even when it paid less than Ignore, i.e. Update preferred)\n')

# Save the validation numbers
dir_valid <- data.frame(
  measure = c('nr P(effort) Ignore', 'nr P(effort) Update', 'nr Ignore-Update paired t',
              'dir P(chose Ignore)', 'dir P(Ignore) vs .5 t', 'dir Update-vs-Ignore IP',
              'dir IP vs 2 t'),
  estimate = c(mean(dplyr::filter(nr_eff_pbo, type == 'Ignore')$p_eff),
               mean(dplyr::filter(nr_eff_pbo, type == 'Update')$p_eff),
               mean(nr_eff_wide$Ignore - nr_eff_wide$Update),
               mean(dir_ign_pbo$p_ignore),
               mean(dir_ign_pbo$p_ignore) - 0.5,
               mean(dir_ip_pbo$IP, na.rm = TRUE),
               mean(dir_ip_pbo$IP, na.rm = TRUE) - 2),
  statistic = c(NA, NA, tt_nr$statistic, NA, tt_dir$statistic, NA, tt_ip$statistic),
  df = c(NA, NA, tt_nr$parameter, NA, tt_dir$parameter, NA, tt_ip$parameter),
  p = c(NA, NA, tt_nr$p.value, NA, tt_dir$p.value, NA, tt_ip$p.value))
write.csv(dir_valid, file.path(deriv_dir, 'dir_type_validation.csv'), row.names = FALSE)
```

Pooled effort analysis: low/no-effort vs high-effort choices (tremor)
```{r}
# Propranolol affects the low-vs-high effort (sz) choices but not the
# effort-vs-no-effort (nr) choices. Pool both into a single "chose the higher-effort
# option" outcome to test (a) whether propranolol has an overall effect on effort
# choice, and (b) whether that effect differs between the two choice types.
# choice==1 = chose the lower-effort option in BOTH tasks (no-redo in nr, sz1 in sz),
# so chose_high_effort = (choice == 0) is consistent across them.
options(buildtools.check = function(action) TRUE)

effort_choice_data <- choice_data_char %>%
  dplyr::filter(tremor_group == 'Yes', task_name %in% c('nr','sz')) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    effort_task       = factor(dplyr::recode(task_name, nr = 'No-effort vs effort',
                                             sz = 'Low vs high effort'),
                               levels = c('Low vs high effort', 'No-effort vs effort')),
    chose_high_effort = as.integer(choice == 0),
    easyOffer_z       = as.numeric(scale(easyOffer)))
# WM-task deviance per cell matched to the pooled model's factors (type x drug).
effort_choice_data <- effort_choice_data %>% dplyr::left_join(
  cw_t_data %>% dplyr::group_by(subNo, type, drug) %>%
    dplyr::summarise(wm_dev = median(dev, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = 'drop'),
  by = c('subNo', 'type', 'drug'))

# Drug is a within-subject manipulation, so include a random slope for drug
# (1+drug_dev|subNo); a random-intercept-only model underestimates the drug SE.
# (a) interaction model, mirroring the single-task choice models: full
# drug_dev*task_dev*type_dev. This both pools the two choice tasks and carries the
# drug x task-type interaction, so it independently verifies the sz finding.
# (Converges, not singular. drug x type p=.010; the 3-way drug x effort_task x type
# is n.s. (p=.16), i.e. the drug x task-type pattern does not differ between tasks.)
## Random effects: maximal supported = (1+drug_dev|subNo) (converges non-singular;
## the fuller drug_dev*task_dev*type_dev random slope is singular). Pooling nr+sz doubles
## the data, so even with this conservative random structure the drug x task-type
## interaction is significant here (OR 2.55, p=.024) -- unlike the sz-only model,
## where it is only a trend. drug x effort_task (nr vs sz) remains null (p=.30).
effort_drug_int <- glmer(chose_high_effort ~ drug_dev*task_dev*type_dev + scale(easyOffer)+scale(updrs_total)+scale(Age)+Gender+ses_order+scale(wm_dev) + (1+drug_dev|subNo),
                         data = add_dev(only_cs(effort_choice_data)), family = binomial,
                         control = glmerControl(optimizer = 'bobyqa',
                                                optCtrl = list(maxfun = 2e5)))
summary(effort_drug_int)

# (b) additive model: pooled propranolol effect on choosing the higher-effort option
effort_drug <- glmer(chose_high_effort ~ drug_dev + task_dev + type_dev + scale(easyOffer)+scale(updrs_total)+scale(Age)+Gender+ses_order+scale(wm_dev) + (1+drug_dev|subNo),
                     data = add_dev(only_cs(effort_choice_data)), family = binomial,
                     control = glmerControl(optimizer = 'bobyqa',
                                            optCtrl = list(maxfun = 2e5)))
summary(effort_drug)

prefix <- 'effort_pooled_tremor'
save(effort_drug_int, effort_drug, file = file.path(deriv_dir, sprintf('%s.RData', prefix)))

# Merged model for the COMBINED choice table, fit on `choice` (==1 = lower-effort
# option) rather than chose_high_effort, so its odds ratios share the polarity of
# the single-task columns (choiceLNp/np/choice_sz_TrLm). Same maximal-supported RE
# as effort_drug_int. This is the exploratory merged-task column.
merged_tab <- glmer(choice ~ drug_dev*task_dev*type_dev + scale(easyOffer)+scale(updrs_total)+scale(Age)+Gender+ses_order+scale(wm_dev) + (1+drug_dev|subNo),
                    data = add_dev(only_cs(effort_choice_data)), family = binomial,
                    control = glmerControl(optimizer = 'bobyqa', optCtrl = list(maxfun = 2e5)))

# Combined choice table: the three single-task decisions plus the exploratory merged
# sz+nr model, side by side. Predictor sets differ, so tab_model unions the terms and
# blanks cells where a predictor is absent. All binomial glmers -> odds ratios; all
# columns model `choice` (==1 = lower-effort / reference option), so ORs are comparable.
make_tab(model = list(choice_sz_TrLm, choiceLNp, np, merged_tab),
         title = 'Table 3. Drug effects on motivation',
         dv_labels = c('High vs low effort', 'Effort vs no effort', 'Ignore vs update', 'High vs no/low effort'),
         directory = deriv_dir)
```
Propranolol simple effects on effort choice, within each task-type
```{r drug-simple-effects, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
## The deviation-coded coefficient tables above give the marginal drug effect and the
## drug x task-type interaction directly. The one thing they cannot show is the
## condition-specific SIMPLE effect (propranolol within Ignore vs within Update) --
## the headline. We recover it with emmeans on the sz and pooled models. The models'
## outcome is `choice` (==1 = LOWER-effort option), so the odds ratio for choosing the
## HIGHER-effort option is exp(-contrast).
library(emmeans)
simple_or <- function(m, lab){
  em <- emmeans(m, ~ drug_dev | type_dev,
                at = list(drug_dev = c(-0.5, 0.5), type_dev = c(-0.5, 0.5)))
  s  <- as.data.frame(summary(pairs(em, reverse = TRUE), infer = c(TRUE, TRUE)))
  data.frame(Model = lab,
             `Task-type` = ifelse(s$type_dev == 0.5, 'Update', 'Ignore'),
             `OR higher-effort` = round(exp(-s$estimate), 2),
             `CI low`  = round(exp(-s$asymp.UCL), 2),
             `CI high` = round(exp(-s$asymp.LCL), 2),
             p = round(s$p.value, 3), check.names = FALSE)
}
drug_simple_effects <- rbind(simple_or(choice_sz_TrLm, 'High-vs-low effort'),
                             simple_or(merged_tab,     'Pooled effort'))
knitr::kable(drug_simple_effects, row.names = FALSE,
             caption = 'Propranolol simple effects (OR for choosing the higher-effort option), by task-type.')
```
Bayesian (brms) confirmation of the drug effects -- Supplementary Table
```{r brms-confirmation, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
## Bayesian confirmation of the drug effects. Guarded by run_brms because brms compiles
## and samples (~15 min; needs Rtools). run_brms = TRUE refits the deviation-coded models
## on the complete-session sample and caches posterior summaries to brms_supp.rds;
## FALSE loads the cache and renders the table. The reported contrasts (marginal drug,
## drug x task-type, propranolol-in-Ignore) are coding-invariant, so the cache is valid.
run_brms   <- FALSE
brms_cache <- file.path(deriv_dir, 'brms_supp.rds')
if (run_brms) {
  suppressMessages({library(brms); library(emmeans)}); options(mc.cores = 4)
  bfit <- function(f, dat, fam) brm(bf(as.formula(f)), data = dat, family = fam,
            chains = 4, iter = 2000, warmup = 1000,
            control = list(adapt_delta = if (identical(fam, gaussian())) .95 else .99),
            seed = 1, refresh = 0, silent = 2)
  cwB <- add_dev(only_cs(cw_t_data)); szB <- add_dev(only_cs(sz_tr_choice_data)); ecB <- add_dev(only_cs(effort_choice_data))
  szB$chose_high_effort <- as.integer(szB$choice == 0)
  covB <- 'scale(easyOffer)+scale(updrs_total)+scale(Age)+Gender+ses_order+scale(wm_dev)'
  bdev <- bfit('dev ~ effort_dev*type_dev*drug_dev + updrs_total_z+ses_order+Gender+age_z+mean_pup_int_z + (1+drug_dev|subNo)', cwB, gaussian())
  brt  <- bfit('rt  ~ effort_dev*type_dev*drug_dev + updrs_total_z+ses_order+Gender+age_z+mean_pup_int_z + (1+drug_dev|subNo)', cwB, gaussian())
  bpup <- bfit('mean_pup ~ effort_dev*type_dev*drug_dev + updrs_total_z+ses_order+Gender+age_z + (1+drug_dev|subNo)', cwB, gaussian())
  bsz  <- bfit(paste0('chose_high_effort ~ drug_dev*type_dev + ', covB, ' + (1+drug_dev|subNo)'), szB, bernoulli())
  bec  <- bfit(paste0('chose_high_effort ~ drug_dev*task_dev*type_dev + ', covB, ' + (1+drug_dev|subNo)'), ecB, bernoulli())
  pdf_ <- function(x){m<-mean(x>0);max(m,1-m)}
  G <- function(ct){s<-as.data.frame(ct);dr<-as.matrix(emmeans::as.mcmc.emmGrid(ct))[,1];setNames(c(s$estimate[1],quantile(dr,.025),quantile(dr,.975),pdf_(dr)),c('est','lo','hi','pd'))}
  dm  <- function(m) G(pairs(emmeans(m,~drug_dev,at=list(drug_dev=c(-.5,.5))),reverse=TRUE))
  di  <- function(m) G(contrast(emmeans(m,~drug_dev*type_dev,at=list(drug_dev=c(-.5,.5),type_dev=c(-.5,.5))),interaction=c('revpairwise','revpairwise')))
  ig  <- function(m){e<-emmeans(m,~drug_dev|type_dev,at=list(drug_dev=c(-.5,.5),type_dev=c(-.5,.5)));ii<-pairs(e,reverse=TRUE);S<-as.matrix(emmeans::as.mcmc.emmGrid(ii));s<-as.data.frame(ii);k<-which(s$type_dev==-.5);setNames(c(s$estimate[k],quantile(S[,k],.025),quantile(S[,k],.975),pdf_(S[,k])),c('est','lo','hi','pd'))}
  brms_supp <- list(dev=dm(bdev), rt=dm(brt), rt_int=di(brt), pup=dm(bpup),
                    sz_int=di(bsz), sz_ign=ig(bsz), ec_int=di(bec), ec_ign=ig(bec))
  saveRDS(brms_supp, brms_cache)
  ## Full, human-readable dump of EVERY fixed-effect posterior (main effects,
  ## interactions and covariates) for every drug model, so any brms result is
  ## accessible without refitting even if it is not cited in the paper.
  full_fixef <- function(fit, label){
    dr <- as.data.frame(fit); cols <- grep('^b_', names(dr), value = TRUE)
    logit <- fit$family$family %in% c('bernoulli','binomial')
    do.call(rbind, lapply(cols, function(pn){ x <- dr[[pn]]
      data.frame(model = label, term = sub('^b_','',pn),
                 median = median(x), est_error = sd(x),
                 lo = unname(quantile(x,.025)), hi = unname(quantile(x,.975)),
                 pd = max(mean(x>0), mean(x<0)),
                 OR_median = if (logit) exp(median(x)) else NA_real_,
                 OR_lo = if (logit) exp(unname(quantile(x,.025))) else NA_real_,
                 OR_hi = if (logit) exp(unname(quantile(x,.975))) else NA_real_,
                 row.names = NULL) })) }
  brms_all_drug <- rbind(
    full_fixef(bdev,'perf_error'), full_fixef(brt,'reaction_time'),
    full_fixef(bpup,'pupil'), full_fixef(bsz,'choice_sz'), full_fixef(bec,'choice_pooled'))
  write.csv(brms_all_drug, file.path(deriv_dir, 'brms_all_fixef_drug.csv'), row.names = FALSE)
  saveRDS(list(dev=bdev, rt=brt, pup=bpup, sz=bsz, ec=bec),
          file.path(deriv_dir, 'brms_drug_fits.rds'))
}
if (file.exists(brms_cache)) {
  bs <- readRDS(brms_cache)
  lin <- function(x,d=2) sprintf('%.*f [%.*f, %.*f]', d, x['est'], d, x[2], d, x[3])
  orr <- function(x)     sprintf('%.2f [%.2f, %.2f]', exp(x['est']), exp(x[2]), exp(x[3]))
  pdv <- function(x)     sprintf('%.3f', x['pd'])
  brms_tab <- data.frame(
    Effect = c('Performance error: propranolol (°)','Reaction time: propranolol (s)',
               'Reaction time: propranolol × task-type (s)','Pupil dilation: propranolol (Z)',
               'Effort choice, sz: propranolol × task-type (OR)','Effort choice, sz: propranolol in Ignore (OR)',
               'Effort choice, pooled: propranolol × task-type (OR)','Effort choice, pooled: propranolol in Ignore (OR)'),
    `Posterior [95% CrI]` = c(lin(bs$dev), lin(bs$rt,3), lin(bs$rt_int,3), lin(bs$pup),
                              orr(bs$sz_int), orr(bs$sz_ign), orr(bs$ec_int), orr(bs$ec_ign)),
    pd = c(pdv(bs$dev),pdv(bs$rt),pdv(bs$rt_int),pdv(bs$pup),pdv(bs$sz_int),pdv(bs$sz_ign),pdv(bs$ec_int),pdv(bs$ec_ign)),
    check.names = FALSE)
  knitr::kable(brms_tab, row.names = FALSE,
               caption = 'Supplemental Table 1. Bayesian (brms) confirmation: posterior median, 95% credible interval, probability of direction (pd).')
} else message('brms cache not found -- set run_brms <- TRUE to fit and cache.')

# Figure: proportion choosing the higher-effort option, by drug and choice type
effort_sum <- effort_choice_data %>% dplyr::group_by(subNo, drug, effort_task) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(p_high = mean(chose_high_effort, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = 'drop')
effort_sum_se <- summarySEwithin(effort_sum, measurevar = 'p_high',

        axis.text = element_text(size = 13))
ggsave(file.path(deriv_dir, 'figures', 'effort_pooled_drug.pdf'), height = 5, width = 8)
```

Paired t-tests: propranolol vs placebo (subject-level)
```{r}
# Simplest test of the drug effect: one value per patient per
# drug, paired PBO vs propranolol (tremor patients with both sessions). These
# corroborate the subject-level mixed models; report them alongside.
paired_t <- function(df, value, label) {
  w <- df %>% dplyr::ungroup() %>% dplyr::select(subNo, drug, val = {{ value }}) %>%
    tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = drug, values_from = val) %>%
    dplyr::filter(!is.na(PBO), !is.na(PROPRANOLOL))
  tt <- t.test(w$PROPRANOLOL, w$PBO, paired = TRUE)
  data.frame(measure = label, N = nrow(w),
             PBO = round(mean(w$PBO), 3), PROPRANOLOL = round(mean(w$PROPRANOLOL), 3),
             diff = round(unname(tt$estimate), 3),
             CI_low = round(tt$conf.int[1], 3), CI_high = round(tt$conf.int[2], 3),
             t = round(unname(tt$statistic), 2), df = unname(tt$parameter),
             p = round(tt$p.value, 3), row.names = NULL)
}

# per-subject x drug summaries (tremor patients, averaged over conditions)
```

Raincloud figures: propranolol vs placebo (ggrain)
```{r}
## Raincloud drug-effect figures (PBO vs PROPRANOLOL) using ggrain::geom_rain.
## Layout per category: jittered points + paired grey lines (left), boxplot (middle),
## half-violin (right); plus a black line joining the two group means.
drug_cols <- c('PBO' = '#1b9e77', 'PROPRANOLOL' = '#d95f02')

make_rain <- function(df, yvar, ylab, fname, width = 5.5) {
  d <- df %>%
    dplyr::ungroup() %>%
    dplyr::select(subNo, drug, y = dplyr::all_of(yvar)) %>%
    dplyr::filter(!is.na(drug), !is.na(y))
  ## keep only subjects with both sessions so the connecting lines are valid
  both <- d %>% dplyr::count(subNo) %>% dplyr::filter(n == 2) %>% dplyr::pull(subNo)
  d <- d %>% dplyr::filter(subNo %in% both) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(drug = factor(drug, levels = c('PBO', 'PROPRANOLOL')))

  p <- ggplot(d, aes(x = drug, y = y, fill = drug, color = drug)) +
    ggrain::geom_rain(
      alpha = .6,
      id.long.var = 'subNo',
      point.args = list(alpha = .6, size = 2),
      line.args = list(alpha = .3, colour = 'grey60'),
      boxplot.args = list(colour = 'black', outlier.shape = NA, width = .12, alpha = .7),
      violin.args = list(colour = NA, alpha = .6)) +
    stat_summary(fun = mean, geom = 'line',  aes(group = 1), colour = 'black', linewidth = .8) +
    stat_summary(fun = mean, geom = 'point', aes(group = 1), colour = 'black', size = 2.4) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = drug_cols) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = drug_cols) +
    scale_x_discrete(labels = c('PBO' = 'PBO', 'PROPRANOLOL' = 'PROPRANOLOL')) +
    theme_classic() +
    labs(x = 'Drug', y = ylab) +
    theme(legend.position = 'none',
          axis.title = element_text(size = 15),
          axis.text  = element_text(size = 12))
  print(p)
  ggsave(file.path(deriv_dir, 'figures', fname), plot = p, height = 5, width = width)
  p
}
```

Pupil time-course ribbons (task-type, effort level, drug)
```{r}
## Time-course pupil ribbons. The raw traces are summarised once to a small per-subject
## binned file (pupil_timecourse.csv, cached below) that is read for the plots.
tc_csv <- file.path(deriv_dir, 'pupil_timecourse.csv')
if (!file.exists(tc_csv)) {
  load(file.path(deriv_dir, 'smooth_pupil_data.RData'))
  pup_tc0 <- smooth_data %>% dplyr::ungroup() %>% dplyr::filter(!is.na(time_bin)) %>%
    dplyr::group_by(subject, session, phase, type, setSize, time_bin) %>%
    dplyr::summarise(mean_pup = mean(pupil_z, na.rm = TRUE), mean_raw = mean(smooth_pup, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = 'drop') %>%
    dplyr::mutate(tbin = as.integer(factor(time_bin)))
  write.csv(pup_tc0, tc_csv, row.names = FALSE); rm(smooth_data); gc()
}
pup_tc <- read.csv(tc_csv) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(phase  = factor(c('1'='Encoding','2'='Delay','3'='Interference')[as.character(phase)],
                                levels = c('Encoding','Delay','Interference')),
                type   = factor(type, levels = c('Ignore','Update')),
                effort = factor(setSize, levels = c(1, 3), labels = c('Low','High')))
# session -> drug for tremor patients (non-tremor have no drug)
drug_long_tc <- drug_list %>% dplyr::select(subNo, drug_ses1, drug_ses2) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_longer(c(drug_ses1, drug_ses2), names_to = 'session', values_to = 'drug', names_pattern = 'drug_ses(.)') %>%
  dplyr::mutate(session = as.integer(session))
pup_tc <- pup_tc %>% dplyr::left_join(drug_long_tc, by = c('subject'='subNo','session'))

# --- TREMOR-DOMINANT ONLY. The non-tremor group is dropped from the manuscript, so every
# time-course pupil analysis below (ribbons, binned LMMs, interference maintenance) is
# restricted to tremor-dominant patients here at the source. ---
td_ids_pup <- part_char %>% dplyr::filter(Tremor_dominant == 'Yes') %>%
  dplyr::pull(SubNr) %>% as.numeric()
pup_tc <- pup_tc %>% dplyr::filter(subject %in% td_ids_pup)

tc_time_labels <- as.character(seq(0.2, 2, 0.2))
# Cousineau-Morey within-subject SE: for each (time, phase) cell, subtract each subject's
# mean across the plotted within-subject conditions and add back the grand mean, then take
# the SE across subjects with the Morey correction sqrt(M/(M-1)) for M conditions. This
# removes the large between-subject pupil-size spread so the ribbon bands reflect the
# WITHIN-subject contrast (effort, task-type, drug -- all repeated within subject). NOT for
# the between-subjects group ribbon, where the between-subject spread IS the effect.
within_se <- function(agg, pos, cond) {
  M <- nrow(dplyr::distinct(agg, dplyr::across(dplyr::all_of(cond))))
  agg %>%
    dplyr::group_by(dplyr::across(dplyr::all_of(pos))) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(gm = mean(val, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
    dplyr::group_by(dplyr::across(dplyr::all_of(c('subject', pos)))) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(sm = mean(val, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
    dplyr::ungroup() %>%
    dplyr::mutate(val_n = val - sm + gm) %>%
    dplyr::group_by(dplyr::across(dplyr::all_of(c(pos, cond)))) %>%
    dplyr::summarise(val = mean(val, na.rm = TRUE),
                     se  = sqrt(M / (M - 1)) * sd(val_n, na.rm = TRUE) / sqrt(dplyr::n()),
                     .groups = 'drop')
}
ribbon_pupil <- function(df, gv, cols, glab, fname, yvar = 'mean_pup', ylab = 'Mean pupil (z-scored)') {
  df <- df %>% dplyr::filter(!is.na(.data[[gv]]), !is.na(.data[[yvar]]))
  # one value per subject per (tbin, phase, gv) cell, then a within-subject (Cousineau-
  # Morey) SE per cell -- gv (effort/task-type/drug) is a within-subject factor.
  agg <- df %>% dplyr::group_by(dplyr::across(dplyr::all_of(c('subject','tbin','phase', gv)))) %>%
    dplyr::summarise(val = mean(.data[[yvar]], na.rm = TRUE), .groups = 'drop')
  s <- within_se(agg, pos = c('tbin','phase'), cond = gv)
  s$tbin <- as.numeric(as.character(s$tbin))
  p <- ggplot(s, aes(x = tbin, y = val, ymin = val - se, ymax = val + se,
                     colour = .data[[gv]], fill = .data[[gv]])) +
    geom_line(linewidth = 1) + geom_ribbon(alpha = .35, colour = NA) +
    facet_wrap(~ phase) + scale_x_continuous(breaks = 1:10, labels = tc_time_labels) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = cols, name = glab) + scale_fill_manual(values = cols, name = glab) +
    theme_classic() + labs(x = 'Time (s)', y = ylab) +
    theme(axis.title = element_text(size = 14), strip.text = element_text(size = 12), legend.position = 'top')
  print(p)
  ggsave(file.path(deriv_dir, 'figures', fname), plot = p, height = 4.5, width = 11)
  ggsave(file.path(deriv_dir, 'figures', sub('\\.pdf$', '.png', fname)), plot = p, height = 4.5, width = 11, dpi = 120)
  p
}
# z-scored ribbons (per-subject z pupil -> between-subject/group SIZE removed)
rib_type   <- ribbon_pupil(pup_tc, 'type',   c('Ignore'='#126192','Update'='#e41e52'), 'Task-type',    'ribbon_pupil_type.pdf')
rib_effort <- ribbon_pupil(pup_tc, 'effort', c('Low'='#2ca02c','High'='#9467bd'),      'Effort level', 'ribbon_pupil_effort.pdf')
rib_drug   <- ribbon_pupil(pup_tc, 'drug',   drug_cols,                                 'Drug',         'ribbon_pupil_drug.pdf')
# raw ribbons (smooth_pup -> retains between-subject/group size differences)

# --- Table representing the ribbons (tremor-dominant only): mixed model on the binned
# time-course pupil (averaged over time within phase), with effort and task-type modulated
# across phases. The non-tremor group is dropped, so this is no longer a between-group table
# -- it characterises how the pupil tracks effort level and task-type (and how that differs
# across encoding/delay/interference) within the tremor-dominant sample. Reported on the
# z-scored (per-subject size-normalised = response SHAPE) signal; the raw-scaling companion
# table was dropped (it added only absolute-size information, redundant with Figure 3A). ---
ribbon_cell <- function(yvar) pup_tc %>%
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(type), !is.na(effort), !is.na(.data[[yvar]])) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(subject, phase, type, effort) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(val = mean(.data[[yvar]], na.rm = TRUE), .groups = 'drop')
pupil_ribbon_lmm <- lmer(val ~ effort*phase + type*phase + (1|subject), data = ribbon_cell('mean_pup'))
make_tab(model = pupil_ribbon_lmm, title = 'Supplemental Table 3. Pupil (z-scored) effort and task-type across phases', directory = deriv_dir, dv_labels = 'Pupil (z-scored)')

# --- 4-ribbon time-course: effort (Low/High) x task-type (Ignore/Update), tremor-dominant.
# Task-type palette (Ignore #126192, Update #e41e52); low-effort ribbons much paler +
# dashed lines, high-effort solid. Faceted by phase. One for z-scored, one for raw. ---
type_cols <- c('Ignore' = '#126192', 'Update' = '#e41e52')
four_ribbon <- function(yvar, ylab, fname) {
  agg <- pup_tc %>% dplyr::filter(!is.na(type), !is.na(effort), !is.na(.data[[yvar]])) %>%
    dplyr::group_by(subject, tbin, phase, type, effort) %>%
    dplyr::summarise(val = mean(.data[[yvar]], na.rm = TRUE), .groups = 'drop')
  s <- within_se(agg, pos = c('tbin','phase'), cond = c('type','effort'))  # 4 within-subject cells
  s$tbin <- as.numeric(as.character(s$tbin))
  p <- ggplot(s, aes(tbin, val, colour = type, group = interaction(type, effort))) +
    geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = val - se, ymax = val + se, fill = type, alpha = effort), colour = NA) +
    geom_line(aes(linetype = effort), linewidth = 1) +
    facet_wrap(~ phase) + scale_x_continuous(breaks = 1:10, labels = tc_time_labels) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = type_cols, name = 'Task-type') +
    scale_fill_manual(values = type_cols, name = 'Task-type') +
    scale_alpha_manual(values = c('Low' = 0.20, 'High' = 0.70), guide = 'none') +
    scale_linetype_manual(values = c('Low' = 'dashed', 'High' = 'solid'), name = 'Effort') +
    theme_classic() + labs(x = 'Time (s)', y = ylab) +
    theme(axis.title = element_text(size = 14), strip.text = element_text(size = 12), legend.position = 'top')
  print(p)
  ggsave(file.path(deriv_dir, 'figures', fname), plot = p, height = 4.5, width = 11)
  ggsave(file.path(deriv_dir, 'figures', sub('\\.pdf$', '.png', fname)), plot = p, height = 4.5, width = 11, dpi = 120)
  p
}
rib_effort_type     <- four_ribbon('mean_pup', 'Mean pupil (z-scored)', 'ribbon_pupil_effort_type.pdf')

# --- TREMOR-DOMINANT figure statistics. Figure 3 A/B (effort effect, task-type interference
# maintenance) are reported within the tremor-dominant sample (the non-tremor group is dropped
# from the manuscript). Whole-trial model parallels fit_pupil() but collapses over drug (both
# sessions pooled), adjusting for UPDRS, age and sex with by-subject random intercepts. ---
cw_all_data <- cw_data_char %>% dplyr::filter(tremor_group == 'Yes', !is.na(mean_pup)) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(age_z = as.numeric(ave(Age, FUN = scale)),
                updrs_z = as.numeric(ave(updrs_total, FUN = scale)))
fit_all <- function(dv) lmer(as.formula(paste0(dv, ' ~ setSize*type + updrs_z + age_z + Gender + (1|subNo)')),
                             data = cw_all_data, control = lmerControl(optimizer = 'bobyqa', optCtrl = list(maxfun = 2e5)))
pupil_all_z   <- fit_all('mean_pup')
pupil_all_raw <- fit_all('mean_raw_pup')
report_terms <- function(m, lab){ cf <- summary(m)$coefficients
  eff  <- grep('^setSize', rownames(cf), value = TRUE); eff <- eff[!grepl(':', eff)][1]
  intx <- grep('^setSize.*:type', rownames(cf), value = TRUE)[1]
  for(t in c(eff, intx)){ i <- which(rownames(cf) == t)
    if(length(i)) cat(sprintf('  %-4s %-22s b=%.3f  t=%.2f  p=%.4g  (N subj=%d)\n',
        lab, t, cf[i,1], cf[i,'t value'], 2*pnorm(-abs(cf[i,'t value'])), lme4::ngrps(m)[['subNo']])) } }
cat('\n=== TREMOR-DOMINANT whole-trial pupil (Figure 3A effort main + effort x task-type) ===\n')
report_terms(pupil_all_z, 'z'); report_terms(pupil_all_raw, 'raw')

# Interference maintenance (Figure 3B), tremor-dominant: task-type x time slope + late-window
# (tbin>=7, ~1.2-2 s) Ignore-vs-Update paired contrast, from the ribbon time-course (pup_tc).
int_tc <- pup_tc %>% dplyr::filter(phase == 'Interference', !is.na(type), !is.na(mean_pup)) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(subject, type, tbin) %>% dplyr::summarise(mp = mean(mean_pup, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = 'drop')
m_int <- lmer(mp ~ type * tbin + (1|subject), data = int_tc)
ci <- summary(m_int)$coefficients; rti <- grep('type.*:tbin|tbin:type', rownames(ci), value = TRUE)[1]
late_int <- int_tc %>% dplyr::filter(tbin >= 7) %>% dplyr::group_by(subject, type) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(mp = mean(mp, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = 'drop') %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = type, values_from = mp) %>% dplyr::filter(!is.na(Ignore), !is.na(Update))
tt_int <- t.test(late_int$Ignore, late_int$Update, paired = TRUE)
cat('\n=== TREMOR-DOMINANT interference maintenance (Figure 3B) ===\n')
cat(sprintf('  task-type x time (%s): b=%.3f t=%.2f p=%.4g\n', rti, ci[rti,1], ci[rti,'t value'], 2*pnorm(-abs(ci[rti,'t value']))))
cat(sprintf('  late window (tbin>=7): Ignore=%.2f Update=%.2f  Delta=%.2f  t(%d)=%.2f  p=%.4g\n',
    mean(late_int$Ignore), mean(late_int$Update), mean(late_int$Ignore - late_int$Update),
    tt_int$parameter, tt_int$statistic, tt_int$p.value))

# --- Eye-tracking availability among tremor-dominant patients (fills the "X participants
# lacking eye-tracking" placeholder in the Participants section). Count TD subjects with
# behavioural (colour-wheel) data vs those with any pupil data. ---
td_char <- cw_data_char %>% dplyr::filter(tremor_group == 'Yes')
n_td_beh <- dplyr::n_distinct(td_char$subNo)
n_td_pup <- dplyr::n_distinct(td_char$subNo[!is.na(td_char$mean_pup)])
cat(sprintf('\n=== Eye-tracking availability (tremor-dominant) ===\n  TD with behaviour=%d, TD with pupil=%d, lacking eye-tracking=%d\n',
    n_td_beh, n_td_pup, n_td_beh - n_td_pup))
cat('  TD subNo lacking pupil:', paste(sort(setdiff(unique(td_char$subNo), unique(td_char$subNo[!is.na(td_char$mean_pup)]))), collapse = ', '), '\n')
```
